main_body: Thatched hip roof over a log-plank front wall with a central door and two round shields
top_band: Thatch roof slope from row 7 to about row 54 (tan #bc9a45 with lighter #d8bb68 course highlights and dark course lines). It sits above the log wall, which is darker and has a different texture.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above. Its outline widens toward the bottom, so the hip slopes read as a surface and not a flat band. It ends in a bright eave edge at rows 52-54 with a dark shadow row under it, then the vertical log wall (rows 55-78). The door is framed and inset with a dark interior. This is the same structure as the Beodeul reference houses, where the roof is the visible top and the wall is the south face. No receding isometric side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 lightness steps with per-course highlights and dotted texture. The log wall has vertical grain in several browns. The outlines are dark brown, tinted to the neighbouring material, and only 6% of dark edge pixels are neutral. There are no flat fills (2% coverage). The candidate is lower than the references on colours per tile (8 vs 11 and 18) and on distinct colours (38 vs 66 and 185). The thatch courses are regular and repetitive. Structure and craft are still close enough to sit next to the references without looking sticker-like.
